prompt: Solve for $x$: $4(x - 2) = 2x + 6$. Give just the number.
hint: Clear the parentheses first. After that it is an equation with $x$ on both sides.

hints.text: Clear the parentheses first. After that it is an equation with $x$ on both sides.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $4(x - 2) = 8$ gives $x - 2 = 2$, so $x = 4$. Yours adds x-terms on the right, so distribute first, then gather the x-terms.
Distributing gives $4x - 8 = 2x + 6$. Subtract $2x$ from both sides, then add $8$ to both sides.
$2x = 14$, and dividing by $2$ gives the solution $x = 7$.

explanation: Distribute the $4$ to both terms inside the parentheses: $4(x - 2) = 4x - 8$.
Subtract $2x$ from both sides to gather the variable on the left: $2x - 8 = 6$.
Add $8$ to both sides to get $2x = 14$, then divide by $2$ to get $x = 7$. Check: $4(7 - 2) = 20$ and $2(7) + 6 = 20$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess-and-check table
steps: Try $x = 5$: left is $4(3) = 12$, right is $16$ — right side wins.
Try $x = 7$: left is $4(5) = 20$, right is $20$ — they tie!
The table shows the sides meet exactly at $x = 7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Writing 4(x − 2) as 4x − 2 forgets to hand the 4 to the second guest in the parentheses.
The outside number multiplies EVERYTHING inside: 4x − 8. Then 4x − 8 = 2x + 6 gives x = 7.
